evidence.title: NIST recommends retaining originals, centralized copies and interpreted logs when evidentiary fidelity matters; comparing protected infrastructure logs can expose changes to system logs.
evidence.observation: NIST recommends retaining originals, centralized copies and interpreted logs when evidentiary fidelity matters; comparing protected infrastructure logs can expose changes to system logs.
evidence.evidence_standing: Foundation guidance inspected; investigative inference, not demonstrated AI behavior
evidence.limitations: Integrity checking addresses later alteration, not original truth or completeness; this latter boundary is the Commons interpretation, not an empirical result. Centralized logging and protected originals can improve recoverability; mirrored logs are not intrinsically deceptive. Historical general guidance, not AI incident evidence; technical algorithm examples are not current cryptographic recommendations.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.
